capsules.description: REST API design conventions: noun-based resources, standard HTTP verbs, idempotency, consistent error schemas (RFC 7807), and pagination.
API Gateway architecture: dynamic routing, mutual TLS (mTLS), JWT validation at the edge, request transformation, and canary traffic splitting.
Handling long-running backend operations: returning HTTP 202 Accepted with a Location header pointing to a pollable status endpoint.
API versioning and format negotiation: URL path versioning vs Accept header versioning, deprecation headers (Sunset RFC 8594), and gzip/brotli.
Standardized API error responses adhering to RFC 9457 Problem Details: type URI, title, status, detail, instance, and machine-readable validation errors.
Enterprise GraphQL: schema design best practices, input object mutations, Relay connection specs, and Apollo Federation.
Hardening production GraphQL: Automatic Persisted Queries (APQ), SHA-256 query whitelisting, disabling introspection in production, and depth limits.
High-throughput binary RPC using gRPC and Protocol Buffers: proto3 syntax, stream multiplexing, and deadline propagation.
Web caching headers: Cache-Control (public, private, immutable), ETag generation, If-None-Match, and 304 Not Modified responses.
Implementing the IETF Idempotency-Key specification for payment and mutation APIs: atomic lock, result storage, and cached response return.
Validating payload structures using standard JSON Schema Draft 2020-12, schema compilation, and compile-time TypeScript type generation.
Building MCP servers conforming strictly to spec 2024-11-05 over stdio or SSE: tools, resources, prompts, prefix pinning, and JSON-RPC 2.0.
Contract-first API development with OpenAPI 3.1: automated TypeScript client generation, mock servers, and breaking change detection.
Keyset and cursor-based pagination for high-volume datasets: eliminating slow OFFSET/LIMIT scans, base64 opaque cursors, and bidirectional navigation.
Algorithmic rate limiting: token bucket for burst traffic, leaky bucket for steady pacing, and sliding window counters.
Robust outbound HTTP client configuration: connection pooling, per-request timeouts, exponential backoff with full jitter, and circuit breaker trips.
Unidirectional real-time streaming with Server-Sent Events (SSE): text/event-stream headers, event IDs for resumption, and LLM token chunks.
Multiplexing multiple channel streams over a single SSE connection, buffer flushing, heartbeat frames, and browser reconnection state.
Reliable webhook publishing and consumption: HMAC-SHA256 signature headers, replay attack protection with timestamps, and exponential backoff.
Full-duplex WebSocket communication: binary frames, heartbeat keep-alive, automatic exponential backoff reconnection, and security.
Supervision hierarchy in actor systems: One-For-One and One-For-All restart strategies, state snapshotting, and fault isolation.
Architectural governance using Nygard ADR format: Context, Decision, Consequences, Status, and living obsidian graph integration.
Protecting domain models from external vendor drift: translating third-party schemas into domain aggregates at the integration boundary.
Lifecycle governance for legacy APIs: deprecation notices, Sunset HTTP headers, telemetry monitoring of remaining traffic, and final shutdown.
Multi-agent coordination architecture: bounding sub-agents (Bel: 5, Enki: 3, Utu: 1, Nabu: 1), prefix-pinned caching, and worktree isolation.
Deterministic Circuit Breaker: closed -> open -> half-open transitions, consecutive failure thresholds, automated reset, and fallback execution.
Strict hexagonal layer decoupling: domain core contains zero framework imports, ports define interfaces, adapters handle external I/O.
AWS / Cloud well-architected framework: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, and cost optimization.
CQRS architecture: separating write models (strict validation, business invariants) from read models (denormalized, optimized for queries).
Disaster recovery strategies (backup/restore, pilot light, warm standby, active-active), automated DNS failover, RTO and RPO metrics.
Distributed synchronization using fencing tokens: monotonically increasing counters to invalidate split-brain writes from delayed clients.
Strategic Domain-Driven Design: context mapping (shared kernel, customer-supplier, conformist), anti-corruption layers, and core domain isolation.
Asynchronous event architecture: domain events, event choreography vs orchestrator-based Sagas, compensating transactions, and idempotency.
Event sourcing: appending immutable domain events, projecting read models via stream replay, and periodically writing state snapshots.
Feature flag governance: release toggles, experiment toggles, kill switches, permission toggles, and automated retirement schedules.
Guaranteeing idempotent message processing in distributed message queues: message ID tracking, atomic upsert checks, and payload hashing.
Microservices architecture: service boundary decomposition, distributed transactions, service discovery, distributed tracing, and resilience.
Modular monolith architecture: clean internal module packages, restricted cross-module exports, in-process event buses, and fast CI builds.
Abstracting cloud infrastructure dependencies (S3/GCS, SQS/PubSub, KMS) behind generic repository interfaces to prevent vendor lock-in.
Multi-tenant architecture: schema-per-tenant, database-per-tenant, and shared schema with PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS).
Bulkhead pattern and service mesh traffic control: allocating isolated thread/connection pools per upstream dependency to prevent cascading failures.
Two-tier caching: in-process L1 cache (Moka/Caffeine, sub-microsecond) backed by distributed L2 cache (Redis), with bus invalidation.
Hierarchical architectural visualization using the C4 model: Context, Containers, Components, and Code diagrams with PlantUML/Mermaid.
Twelve-Factor app methodology: codebase, dependencies, config in environment, backing services as resources, stateless processes, concurrency.
Establishing ubiquitous domain language: resolving ambiguity, mapping terms across domain boundaries, and maintaining living terminology contracts.
Zero-trust network architecture: mutual TLS between all internal services, cryptographically verified service identities (SPIFFE/SPIRE), and explicit authorization.
Production authentication: OAuth2 Authorization Code Flow with PKCE, rotating short-lived JWTs, secure HTTP-only cookies, and refresh token revocation.
Distributed background job processing with BullMQ and Celery: exponential backoff retries, dead letter queues (DLQ), and idempotency keys.
Robust POSIX Shell and Bash scripting: strict error modes (set -euo pipefail), signal cleanup traps, robust CLI flag parsing with getopts, and variable quoting.
Production CLI tool design: sub-millisecond startup, subcommands, POSIX flags with clap/cobra, progress indicators, and standard exit codes.
Code maintainability heuristics: 7±2 rule of working memory, flattening cyclomatic complexity, early returns, and parse-don't-validate.
Actor-based concurrency systems: message passing, mailbox backpressure, lock-free state isolation, and zero race conditions.
Modern C++20: RAII memory management, smart pointers (std::unique_ptr, std::shared_ptr), concepts, and move semantics.
Dart 3+ engineering: sound null-safety, exhaustive pattern matching, reactive Streams, multi-threaded Isolates for CPU-heavy tasks, and robust CLI/backend architecture.
High-traffic caching: probabilistic early expiration (XFetch), mutex locks on cache miss to prevent dogpiling/thundering herd, and cache tagging.
Production Django & Django REST Framework: select_related/prefetch_related optimization, custom auth models, and Celery.
Tactical and strategic domain modeling: aggregate roots, value objects, domain events, invariants boundary enforcement, and pure business logic.
C# 13 and .NET 9: MediatR CQRS, Entity Framework Core query splitting, Minimal APIs, and ValueTask allocations.
Elixir and Phoenix: Erlang/OTP actor model, supervision trees, GenServer state, Ecto migrations, and LiveView channels.
Embedded firmware and C/Rust bare-metal development: no_std, static memory allocation, DMA, interrupt service routines, and power efficiency.
Enterprise Express.js API design: modular routing, secure middleware chaining with Helmet and CORS, centralized async error-handling middleware, Zod request validation, and graceful shutdown.
High-throughput FastAPI microservices: dependency injection, OpenAPI auto-docs, async database sessions, and streaming.
Flask 3+ Python microservices: modular Blueprints architecture, Application Factory pattern, SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM integration, Pydantic validation, and isolated Pytest fixtures.
Idiomatic Go: goroutines, channels, sync.WaitGroup, context propagation, table-driven tests, and sub-millisecond HTTP microservices.
Solving N+1 query problems in GraphQL APIs using DataLoader batching, memoization caches, and Apollo Federation v2 subgraphs.
Production gRPC microservices: protobuf schema backward compatibility rules, bidirectional streaming, interceptors, and client-side load balancing.
Kotlin 2.0: structured concurrency with Coroutines and Flow, Ktor backend microservices, and Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP).
Laravel 11+ enterprise development: Eloquent ORM relations and query scopes, Artisan console automation, asynchronous background Queues and Jobs, Livewire components, and Service Providers.
Incremental legacy modernization using the Strangler Fig pattern, anti-corruption layers (ACL), parallel run verification, and zero downtime.
Lua 5.4 and LuaJIT systems programming: metatable object orientation, functional lexical closures, coroutine cooperative multitasking, and high-performance embedding within C/C++.

NestJS enterprise architecture: modular design, controllers, services, guards, interceptors, pipes, and TypeORM/Prisma.
Node.js runtime performance: avoiding event loop lag, libuv thread pool tuning, Worker Threads for CPU intensive tasks, and memory heap profiling.

Modern Python 3.12+: strict type hints, asyncio concurrency, Pydantic v2 schemas, pytest fixtures, and GIL considerations.
Modern R scientific computing: Tidyverse functional paradigms, high-performance data.table manipulation, ggplot2 data visualization, and reproducible environments with renv.
Ruby on Rails conventions, ActiveRecord transaction blocks, Sidekiq background jobs, Hotwire/Turbo, and Sorbet typing.
Distributed rate limiting algorithms: sliding window logs with Redis sorted sets, token bucket with Lua scripts, and client fingerprinting.
Idiomatic Rust, borrow checker mastery, zero-cost abstractions, Tokio async runtime, and robust Error handling with thiserror.
Spring Boot 3, Java 21 Virtual Threads, Spring Security 6, Spring Data JPA, and GraalVM Native Image compilation.

Advanced TypeScript: nominal Branded Types, conditional types, mapped types, template literal types, and strict AST compilation.
Horizontally scaled stateful WebSockets: Redis adapter for broadcast, connection drain on shutdown, heartbeat ping-pong, and reconnection state recovery.
Understanding Read Committed, Repeatable Read, and Serializable: preventing dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, phantom reads, and write skew.
Point-In-Time Recovery (PITR): base backups, continuous WAL archiving to S3, pg_dump strategies, and automated recovery drills.
Apache Cassandra distributed architecture: Cassandra Query Language (CQL), query-first data modeling, Partition Key and Clustering Column optimization, tunable consistency, and tombstone mitigation.
Transactional Outbox pattern and Change Data Capture via Debezium: guaranteed at-least-once event publication from database WAL logs.
Columnar storage for billion-row aggregations: MergeTree table engines, primary key sorting, sparse indexing, and materialized views.
Formulaic connection pool sizing: pool size = (core_count * 2) + effective_spindle_count, connection timeout limits, and leak detection.
Data privacy in persistence: deterministic pseudonymization, cryptographic hashing of identifiers, automated PII scrubbing, and hard deletion.
Relational query optimization: covering indexes, eliminating sequential scans, query plan cost analysis, and composite index ordering.
Preventing database deadlocks: acquiring locks in globally deterministic alphabetical order, short transaction scopes, and retry loops.
Drizzle ORM: zero-overhead type-safe SQL queries, relations query builder, drizzle-kit schema migrations, and prepared statements.
Amazon DynamoDB serverless architecture: Single-Table Design, Composite Partition and Sort Keys (PK/SK), Global Secondary Indices (GSI), conditional writes, and RCU/WCU cost optimization.

Graph data modeling: nodes, relationships, properties, Cypher traversal optimization, and index-free adjacency.

Horizontal table partitioning (range, list, hash) in PostgreSQL, shard key selection, cross-partition query elimination, and read replicas.

SQLite WAL mode (synchronous = NORMAL), single-writer MPSC queue architecture, zero SQLITE_BUSY, and FTS5 search indexes.

Production Docker: multi-stage builds, rootless execution, distroless minimal base images, and .dockerignore optimization.

FinOps cloud financial management: mandatory resource cost tagging, Kubernetes request/limit rightsizing, and automated idle teardown.
High-performance structured logging: Fluent Bit daemonset, JSON log parsing, multiline exception handling, and OpenSearch/Loki shipping.

GitLab CI/CD pipeline automation: .gitlab-ci.yml DAG stages, Docker-in-Docker runners, multi-project pipeline triggers, caching strategies, and protected environments with approval gates.

Observability metrics: Prometheus Four Golden Signals (Latency, Traffic, Errors, Saturation), Alertmanager routing, and Grafana panels.

OWASP Zero-Trust security rules prohibiting unparameterized raw SQL, eval(), dangerouslySetInnerHTML, and hardcoded credential leaks.

File watcher hook: upon file save in src/, runs associated unit test in tests/ within isolated sandbox and reports diagnostics.
Obsidian vault synchronization hook: after successful task completion, checks if architectural contracts or ADRs need updating.
Runtime interceptor: monitors interactive database transactions, aborting any transaction that exceeds 25ms or makes network calls.
Lexical cleaner hook: removes non-standard Unicode punctuation (em-dashes, smart quotes) from source code before passing to compilers.
Cost guard hook: alerts when a tool call exceeds typical latency (e.g. web scraping, heavy embeddings) and demands confirmation.
Loop detection interceptor: tracks file edit diff hashes; if an agent alternates between identical states across turns, execution is aborted.
Egress filter: scans terminal output, error logs, and commit messages for API keys (sk-, ghp_, AKIA) and masks them with [REDACTED].

Session conclusion hook: aggregates elapsed time, tokens consumed, test pass ratio, and computes MTTR for the live dashboard.
Turn interceptor: tracks milestones in working.md, updating completed checkboxes [x] and preserving current intent across session boundaries.
